title: Java Silently Truncates Integer Division (Here's the Fix)
description:
Divide two ints in Java and the decimal just disappears -- no warning, no error. In under a minute, see why int / int always truncates, how casting to double fixes it, and why casting a double to int never rounds either.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/java-mastery-path/level-1/02-variables-data-types/

#Shorts

beats.narration: In Java, dividing two whole numbers doesn't round -- it just throws the decimal away. No warning. No error. Just silence.

display.heading: Integer Division
display.subheading: Java Mastery Path -- Level 1: Variables & Operators

beats.narration: Ten divided by three should be three point three three. Java prints three, because int divided by int always gives you an int.
Cast one side to a double before you divide, and Java keeps every decimal you actually wanted.
And casting a double to an int isn't rounding either -- nineteen ninety nine becomes nineteen flat, every time.
Variables, types, casting -- it's all in lesson two. Full code's linked right below.
